question.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (8-\lambda )(2-\lambda ) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =8,\,2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{8} \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$
